newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. food agency urges end to Zaire refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food agency urges end to Zaire refugee crisis.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme appealed on Friday for an urgent political solution to the refugee crisis in eastern Zaire, saying the cost of delivering aid was becoming unsustainable.

Catherine Bertini, head of the Rome-based agency, said in a statement that the cost of delivering food was 10 times higher than normal because rough terrain had made the use of air transport obligatory.

"In the absence of a political solution, it is difficult to see how relief agencies like WFP can sustain such an expensive and complicated relief effort over a long period of time," Bertini was quoted as saying.
"While we have no intention to pull out, we have been forced to look at new ways of delivering food to the region, but even these are very expensive," she added.
"This is not a problem that can be solved by humanitarian agencies...a long-term political solution requires diplomacy as well as generosity on the part of the donor community in the short-term."

The statement said some 200,000 refugees were located near the towns of Tingi Tingi, Lubutu, Amisi and Shabunda and that security problems were preventing the WFP delivering food overland from Rwanda.
"At the same time, armed militias among the refugees are preventing civilians from returning to their homes in Rwanda," the statement said.
Rebel advances in eastern Zaire last October uprooted more than a million refugees who had fled to Zaire after civil war and the massacre of up to a million people in Rwanda in 1994.
